patients.summary: Administrative assistant with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis and SSc-associated PAH who joins in 2020, develops hypertension that becomes refractory and is found to be a pheochromocytoma with cortisol excess, then has nickel contact dermatitis, a hysterectomy complicated by ureteral injury, PAH progression, scleroderma renal crisis and, after her last visit, septic shock.

conditions.label: Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with systemic sclerosis
conditions.note: Diagnosed at outside pulmonary hypertension clinic; on sildenafil

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth daily before breakfast

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34 y/o woman establishing care. Her last primary care office was out of the area and she wants someone closer to home and work (admin assistant).

PMH:
- Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis, dx 2018 by an outside rheumatology group, which she still sees once a year. Skin tightness of hands/forearms and trunk, stable per her.
- Pulmonary arterial hypertension, felt to be SSc-related, diagnosed 2019 at an outside PH clinic. On sildenafil 20 mg TID. Followed by PH cardiology yearly. Walks without trouble on flat ground.
- Heartburn, takes omeprazole 20 daily, controlled.
PSH: none.
Meds: sildenafil 20 mg TID, omeprazole 20 mg daily.
Allergies: nickel - itchy rash under cheap earrings and belt buckles. No drug allergies.
FHx: mother has lupus. Father has high blood pressure. No known adrenal tumors, endocrine tumor syndromes or neurofibromatosis in the family.
SHx: never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs. Lives in Amherst. Works full time at a desk.

ROS: no chest pain, no syncope, no edema, no dysphagia beyond occasional heartburn. Periods regular.

Exam: BP and vitals as recorded, normal today. Well appearing. Skin: thickened, shiny skin over fingers and dorsal hands, forearms; no ulcers. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. No edema.

A/P
1. Diffuse SSc - stable, rheum following. Will get their letters.
2. PAH on sildenafil - PH clinic following. Records request sent.
3. Health maintenance: Tdap today. HIV and hep C screening once, she agrees. Labs: CBC, CMP, UA, lipids. Pap was 2019 at her old office, records requested. PHQ-2 negative.
RTC 6 months or with the physical next fall.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Susan, all of your labs from Monday look good. Kidney function, blood counts, liver tests and cholesterol are in the normal range, and your urine showed no protein or blood. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Nice to meet you.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care office

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records packet from the patient's previous primary care office, 2016 to 2020. Summary of contents:
- Problem list: systemic sclerosis, diffuse cutaneous (rheumatology, 2018); pulmonary arterial hypertension (PH clinic, 2019); heartburn.
- Medications: sildenafil 20 mg three times a day; omeprazole 20 mg daily.
- Allergies: nickel (contact rash). NKDA.
- Cervical cytology 2019: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, HPV negative.
- BP readings 2017 to 2020 all below 130/80.
- Annual influenza vaccines through 2019.
Reviewed and abstracted by PCP. Scanned to media.

documents.title: Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here before work for flu shot. Afebrile, feeling well. Screening questions negative. Quadrivalent flu given IM left deltoid, lot recorded. Waited 15 min, no reaction. VIS given.

documents.title: Sildenafil PA Renewal
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Insurer sent PA renewal for sildenafil 20 mg TID, dx pulmonary arterial hypertension. Original approval came through the PH clinic; insurer now wants PCP of record to sign. Submitted with PH clinic note from 2019 and our 9/14 visit note. Approved 11/11 for 12 months. Pharmacy notified.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 2021-03-22

Dear colleague,
I saw Ms. Jean-Baptiste for her yearly review of diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis. She feels well. Skin thickening over the hands, forearms and anterior chest is unchanged from last year by my exam. No digital ulcers. No new joint, muscle or bowel complaints. Breathing unchanged, PH team following.
BP 118/76 in clinic. Creatinine 0.9 last fall per your labs, which I reviewed.
Current medications: sildenafil 20 mg three times daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily. Allergy: nickel.
Assessment: stable disease. No change to treatment today. I asked her to keep having blood pressure and kidney function checked with you and to call us for any sudden rise in pressure or headache.
Return in one year.
Rheumatology

events.reason: Follow-up, elevated blood pressure at pharmacy

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Checked her BP on the machine at the grocery pharmacy twice last month and got 140s/90s, came in to have it looked at. No headache, no chest pain, no vision changes. Feels fine. Rheum visit last month was stable.

O: BP 146/94, repeat after 5 min seated 144/92. HR regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P: Elevated BP on two occasions, new for her (prior records all normal). Father has HTN. In someone with SSc I don't want to sit on this. Asked her to buy an upper-arm cuff and log mornings and evenings for two weeks, then video visit to review. Reviewed when to call: severe headache, vision change, BP over 180/110.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she is on her lunch break in her car. Confirmed name and DOB.

Home log 4/14-5/14 with an Omron upper-arm cuff: average about 142/90, range 134-151 over 86-96. Technique reviewed with her on camera, looks right. No symptoms.

A: Essential hypertension. Normal kidney function and UA in September.
P: Start amlodipine 5 mg daily. Mentioned ankle swelling as a possible side effect. Recheck in clinic in 3 months with the log. Rx sent.

documents.title: Pulmonary Hypertension Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, pulmonary hypertension program
Visit: 2021-06-21

Re: Susan Jean-Baptiste
Annual review of SSc-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension. Functionally she is unchanged: manages a flight of stairs and her usual walking without stopping. No syncope, no chest pain, no edema.
New since last year: her PCP started amlodipine 5 mg for hypertension; no objection from us.
Exam: BP 128/80, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air. JVP not raised. Heart sounds regular. Lungs clear. No peripheral edema.
Medications: sildenafil 20 mg TID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily. Allergy: nickel.
Impression: stable PAH on sildenafil monotherapy.
Plan: continue sildenafil 20 mg TID. See her in a year, sooner for any change in exercise tolerance.
Cardiology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Hypertension Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Taking amlodipine every morning. No ankle swelling. Home readings mostly 134-140/84-90.
BP here 138/88. Exam otherwise unchanged, no edema.
Still above goal. Increase amlodipine to 10 mg daily. She'll use up the 5s by taking two. Physical in October with labs.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 35F.

Interval: amlodipine went to 10 in August, tolerating it. Home BPs now 120s-130s/80s. Rheum (March) and PH clinic (June) both stable. Breathing unchanged, no edema. Periods regular. Mood good, PHQ-2 0. Busy at work.

Meds: amlodipine 10 daily, sildenafil 20 TID, omeprazole 20 daily. Allergies: nickel.

Exam: BP 132/84. Well. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal size. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Skin with sclerodactyly and forearm thickening, unchanged, no ulcers. No edema. Breasts deferred at her request - no concerns.

A/P
- HTN: much better, continue.
- SSc / PAH: specialists following.
- Prevention: flu today; PCV20 today given her PAH. Pap up to date (2019, HPV neg), next due 2024. COVID booster when eligible - she plans to go to the pharmacy. Labs: CMP, CBC, UA, lipids, TSH.
Return 6 months for BP.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Susan - all normal. Kidneys and potassium fine on the amlodipine, thyroid normal, cholesterol good, urine clear. See you in the spring.
